name: Cigarettemaxxing

card.summary: A fringe idea that smoking cigarettes can debloat the face or suppress appetite and so produce a leaner-looking face.
card.note: Smoking is associated with documented facial aging and serious disease.

quick.overview:
Cigarettemaxxing is the term for smoking as an appearance tactic. Proponents hope for two payoffs: a leaner, less puffy face through lower appetite and body weight, and a more hollowed look to the cheeks.

In the research literature, smoking is linked to lower body weight on average and, separately, to earlier visible facial aging. Studies of identical twins that differed in smoking history found more wrinkles, eyelid sagging, under-eye bags and jowls in the smoking twin. Nobody has trialled smoking as a debloating method.
quick.how: Users who discuss it describe it as a cigarette habit adopted to reduce appetite or to change facial softness. It is usually raised as a question or last resort by people who report persistent facial bloat despite low body fat, rather than as an established protocol.
quick.risks: Tobacco smoking is a leading cause of preventable death and causes cancers, heart disease and lung disease. Dermatology and plastic-surgery research associates it with premature wrinkling, sagging and bags. Nicotine is addictive, and quitting is commonly followed by appetite and weight rebound.

lead: Cigarettemaxxing is a term from looksmaxxing forums for taking up smoking in order to change one's appearance, chiefly by debloating the face or reducing appetite and body weight.[1] It sits at the fringe of the community and is usually discussed as a controversial question rather than a recommended method.

The idea rests on two beliefs. One is that smoking suppresses appetite and so lowers weight and facial fat. The other, voiced in a forum thread, is that smoking 'accelerates aging' and degrades facial fat pads, which the poster presented as a way to look more gaunt.[1] Thread respondents were largely hostile to the idea.[1]

Published research on smoking and the face concerns the opposite of a cosmetic benefit: twin studies report more visible aging in the smoking twin.[2] No study has tested smoking as a debloating technique.

chain: Smoking suppresses appetite and lowers average body weight
Less facial fat and puffiness is expected
angle.text: Proponents hope smoking leads to a leaner face by reducing appetite, or by thinning facial fat. Research instead associates smoking with earlier wrinkling, sagging and under-eye bags.

paras: The term combines 'cigarette' with the '-maxxing' suffix used across looksmaxxing for optimizing a feature. In one looksmax.org thread, a user with very low body fat but persistent facial bloat asked whether cigarettemaxxing could help, saying he had seen a claim on another forum that it worked.[1] He said ordinary advice such as drinking water, gym work and potassium had been difficult for him to apply.[1]
Replies in that thread were mostly dismissive or hostile, and the poster described himself as desperate for a solution.[1]
The reasoning offered is that smoking accelerates aging and breaks down facial fat pads, producing a thinner face, and that it also lowers appetite.[1]

In a twin study reported in 2013, plastic surgeons who did not know smoking histories graded photographs of 79 pairs of identical twins in which one twin smoked or had smoked at least five years longer. The smoking twins showed more upper-eyelid sagging, under-eye bags, nasolabial lines, lip wrinkles and jowls, especially in the lower two-thirds of the face, and the surgeons could usually tell which twin smoked.[2]

Tobacco smoke contains thousands of chemicals, many of them carcinogens, and smoking is described as the leading cause of preventable death, causing lung and other cancers, heart attacks, stroke and chronic lung disease.[3]
No studies found on cigarettemaxxing itself. Related research on smoking and facial aging (twin photo-grading studies) reports more wrinkling and sagging in smokers.[2]

lore.intro: The idea appears in occasional looksmax.org threads and is typically met with strong pushback from other members.[1]

claims.claim: Smoking debloats the face by degrading fat pads
claims.believers: A poster relayed a claim from another forum that smoking works for debloating because it accelerates aging and degrades facial fat pads.[1]
claims.experts: A twin study found more eyelid sagging, bags, lip wrinkles and jowls in the smoking twin; it did not test debloating.[2]

claims.claim: Smoking suppresses appetite and keeps the face lean
claims.believers: Proponents of smoking for weight control say it reduces hunger and keeps body fat low; the forum poster linked the idea to facial leanness.[1]
claims.experts: No published trial has tested smoking as a facial slimming method; health bodies document major disease risks of smoking.[3]
